description:
Approved by the user 2026-11-17 (relayed by JSON) from the JSON machine-code study (fz vs BEAM JIT, lldb single-step traces). Study files: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/ebbfffd8-2561-4da7-bcda-f9a316d00a1e/scratchpad/jsonasm/ (listings/, listings/beam/, CLIF dumps).

Evidence: each literal clause test re-derives the tag check, length load, -1 sentinel compare, bounds check, data-pointer load, alignment test and byte load (13-20 instructions each). val's { path repeats this five times before its final one-byte select: 228 instructions vs BEAM ~70 (one bs_start_match3, one ensure_at_least, one read, then select_val).

Source: lower_bitstring_region (src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs ~4048) emits per-region BitstringBitLen / IsNotBinary / BitFieldFits / BitReadByteIntAt; prim.rs emit_binary_bit_len (778), emit_binary_base (795), emit_int_read_at_bit (965); the redundant ule 8,64 constant compare.

Concordant evidence: Make Distiller Fast's byte walk (after fz-sc8.247) still re-tests the binary's layout three times and its alignment twice per byte (~19 of 61 instructions); carrying the byte pointer and bit length with the cursor makes them loop-invariant. fz-sc8.183.4 (one implementation of bounds arithmetic) is the same seam.

Done when: a fixture or CLIF pin counts binary region reads in a multi-literal dispatch at one per function entry; three paths agree.

Order: after fz-nml.27 (same lowering, in flight).

comments.text: Concordant evidence 2026-11-18 (Make Distiller Fast, bench profile at develop 37c5473cd, per-instruction sampler, 110k samples). The JSON string scanner (lib/json.fz string/3) is 11.9% inclusive and 8.3-9.9% self. Clauses 1-2 match a one-byte literal segment, clauses 3-4 bind c with a guard, and the dispatch reads the same position once for each kind. Per byte it loads the binary's size twice, its data pointer twice and the byte twice, bounds-checks twice, and branches on the representation tag about five times. .248 step 1 does not change this loop. skip_ws (2.2% self) has the same shape. Tools: bench distill-hunt pcprof.c/pcsum.py/hot.py.

title: A binary match reads its region once, and sibling literal clauses become one byte decision
